info.title: apid
info.description: The appliance management API served over HTTPS on the device.

post.description:
Requires the current password. Answers **204** on success; every session
but the acting one is dropped. A wrong current password is **401**, and a
new password below the length floor is **422**.

204.description: The password was changed; every session except the calling one was dropped

400.description: The body is not JSON, or not this shape (`request_invalid`)

401.description: No stored bearer token or authenticated browser session (`not_authenticated`)

403.description: The browser CSRF token is invalid (`csrf_invalid`), or the current password does not verify (`wrong_password`)

405.description: A method this route does not serve (`method_not_allowed`); carries `Allow`

422.description: The new password is shorter than 8 characters (`validation_failed`)

500.description: Hashing failed (`hashing_failed`), or mosd failed to answer (`settings_io`, `mosd_failed`)

503.description: The call to mosd could not be made (`mosd_unreachable`); carries `Retry-After`

504.description: The bounded call to mosd timed out (`mosd_timeout`); the operation may still be running

post.description:
Answers **202**: the request is accepted and the power-off is dispatched,
so there may be no connection left to carry a later status.

202.description: The power-off was accepted and dispatched; the call to mosd is not awaited, so completion is not reported over this connection

401.description: No stored bearer token or authenticated browser session (`not_authenticated`)

403.description: A browser session mutation omitted or supplied the wrong CSRF token (`csrf_invalid`)

405.description: A method this route does not serve (`method_not_allowed`); carries `Allow`

post.description:
Answers **202**: the request is accepted and the reboot is dispatched, so
there may be no connection left to carry a later status.

202.description: The reboot was accepted and dispatched; the call to mosd is not awaited, so completion is not reported over this connection

401.description: No stored bearer token or authenticated browser session (`not_authenticated`)

403.description: A browser session mutation omitted or supplied the wrong CSRF token (`csrf_invalid`)

405.description: A method this route does not serve (`method_not_allowed`); carries `Allow`

post.description:
The password must be 8 to 72 bytes and contain no NUL, newline or carriage
return. 72 is bcrypt's limit — a longer password would be silently
truncated, so it is refused instead.

The password is written into no setting, is never logged, and lasts until
the next reboot. A **422** states which bound was broken and never repeats
the password back.

Answers **202** once the password hash is written and its scoped apply is queued.

202.description: The transient root password hash was written and its scoped apply was queued

400.description: The body is not JSON, or not this shape (`request_invalid`)

401.description: No stored bearer token or authenticated browser session (`not_authenticated`)

403.description: A browser session mutation omitted or supplied the wrong CSRF token (`csrf_invalid`)

405.description: A method this route does not serve (`method_not_allowed`); carries `Allow`

422.description: The password is shorter than 8 bytes, longer than 72, or contains a NUL, newline or carriage return (`validation_failed`); the message states the bound and never the password

500.description: mosd failed to set it (`mosd_failed`)

503.description: The call to mosd could not be made (`mosd_unreachable`); carries `Retry-After`

504.description: The bounded call to mosd timed out (`mosd_timeout`); the operation may still be running

post.summary: Rotate a WireGuard interface's private key.
post.description:
An action rather than a settings write: the private key lives in a
mode-0640 file on STATE that the settings tree does not describe. mosd
draws a new key, tears down the device holding the old one and reconciles.

Answers **200** with the new public key — the tunnel is already running on
it. The private half is never returned. **404** when `iface` names no
declared `network` entry; **422** when the entry exists but is not of kind
`wireguard`.

parameters.name: iface
parameters.description: The `network` entry to rotate, which must be one of kind `wireguard`: `wg0`

200.description: A new key was drawn; the body carries its public half

401.description: No stored bearer token or authenticated browser session (`not_authenticated`)

403.description: A browser session mutation omitted or supplied the wrong CSRF token (`csrf_invalid`)

404.description: The name is not a declared `network` entry (`settings_not_found`); the URL names no interface to rotate

405.description: A method this route does not serve (`method_not_allowed`); carries `Allow`

422.description: The entry exists and is not a WireGuard one (`settings_rejected`)

500.description: mosd failed to rotate (`settings_io`, `mosd_failed`)

503.description: The call to mosd could not be made (`mosd_unreachable`); carries `Retry-After`

504.description: The bounded call to mosd timed out (`mosd_timeout`); the operation may still be running

get.summary: Report whether this appliance is manageable.
get.description:
Answers **200 in every state**, including when mosd is unreachable — a
failure is reported in the body, never as a status code, so it cannot be
confused with this endpoint being down. mosd's state is determined by one
live bus call per request.

Authenticated. For plain listener liveness use the unauthenticated
`/healthz` instead; neither answer implies the other.

200.description: Whether this appliance is manageable. **200 in both states**: a dead mosd is reported as `mosd: "unreachable"` in the body, never as a status code

401.description: No stored bearer token or authenticated browser session (`not_authenticated`)

405.description: A method this route does not serve (`method_not_allowed`); carries `Allow`

get.summary: Report what the caller is talking to.
get.description:
Answers the API major version, the daemon name, and
`settingsSchemaVersion` — the shape of the settings tree on disk, which
moves independently of the API version. Authenticated.

200.description: What this daemon is and which schema it speaks

401.description: No stored bearer token or authenticated browser session (`not_authenticated`)

405.description: A method this route does not serve (`method_not_allowed`); carries `Allow`

get.summary: Read declared network configuration together with current link state.

200.description: Configured interfaces and the current systemd-networkd observation

401.description: No API credential was supplied

500.description: The configured network map could not be read

503.description: mosd is unavailable

504.description: The bounded call to mosd timed out

put.summary: Replace the whole interface map, validated as one tree.
put.description:
The only way to make two interdependent entries legal in one step: adding a
bridge and its ports through the per-interface route means declaring the
ports first, because a bridge naming an undeclared port is refused.

Answers **422** with the failing rule's own message when the map does not
validate; nothing is written in that case.

204.description: The map was replaced; the reconciler has re-rendered every unit from it

401.description: No stored bearer token or authenticated browser session (`not_authenticated`)

403.description: A browser session mutation omitted or supplied the wrong CSRF token (`csrf_invalid`)

405.description: A method this route does not serve (`method_not_allowed`); carries `Allow`

422.description: The body is not a map of interfaces, a key is not an interface name, an entry declares a static address that is not IPv4 CIDR notation, or a relational rule refuses it -- a VLAN parent or a bridge port that is not a declared entry, a bridge port carrying addressing, a port claimed twice (`validation_failed`); or mosd rejected the write (`settings_rejected`)

500.description: mosd failed to write (`settings_io`, `mosd_failed`)

503.description: The call to mosd could not be made (`mosd_unreachable`); carries `Retry-After`

504.description: The bounded call to mosd timed out (`mosd_timeout`); the operation may still be running

put.summary: Declare or replace one interface, validated against the whole map.
put.description:
**A `PUT` replaces the entry entirely**, including a tunnel's peer list: a
body with no `wireguard` block on an interface that had one leaves it with
none. To change one field, send the whole entry.

Creates the interface when it does not exist, so there is no 404. A name
outside the interface charset, or a map that fails validation, is **422**.

parameters.name: iface
parameters.description: The interface to declare or replace: `eth0`, or `eth0.100` for a VLAN. Created when it does not exist

204.description: The entry was written; the reconciler has re-rendered its units

401.description: No stored bearer token or authenticated browser session (`not_authenticated`)

403.description: A browser session mutation omitted or supplied the wrong CSRF token (`csrf_invalid`)

405.description: A method this route does not serve (`method_not_allowed`); carries `Allow`

422.description: The name is not an interface name, the body is not an interface, the entry declares a static address that is not IPv4 CIDR notation, or a relational rule refuses the resulting map (`validation_failed`); or mosd rejected the write (`settings_rejected`)

500.description: The stored map holds an entry this build cannot read (`settings_invalid`), or mosd failed (`settings_io`, `mosd_failed`)

503.description: The call to mosd could not be made (`mosd_unreachable`); carries `Retry-After`

504.description: The bounded call to mosd timed out (`mosd_timeout`); the operation may still be running

delete.summary: Remove one interface, re-validating the rest of the map without it.
delete.description:
Removing an interface another entry depends on — a port still listed by a
bridge — is **422** with the failing rule's own message, and nothing is
written. Remove the dependent reference first.

Read-modify-write: two concurrent removals lose one.

204.description: The entry was removed; the reconciler has swept its units

401.description: No stored bearer token or authenticated browser session (`not_authenticated`)

403.description: A browser session mutation omitted or supplied the wrong CSRF token (`csrf_invalid`)

404.description: No `network` entry has that name (`settings_not_found`). Well-formed and absent, which is a different answer from malformed

405.description: A method this route does not serve (`method_not_allowed`); carries `Allow`

422.description: The name is not an interface name, or removing the entry breaks a relational rule -- a bridge still lists it as a port, a VLAN still names it as a parent (`validation_failed`)

500.description: The stored map holds an entry this build cannot read (`settings_invalid`), or mosd failed (`settings_io`, `mosd_failed`)

503.description: The call to mosd could not be made (`mosd_unreachable`); carries `Retry-After`

504.description: The bounded call to mosd timed out (`mosd_timeout`); the operation may still be running

get.summary: List every peer configured on one WireGuard tunnel.
get.description: Answers **404** when `iface` names no declared interface.

200.description: The stored peers, in stored order, each with the public key that is its `DELETE` path segment

401.description: No stored bearer token or authenticated browser session (`not_authenticated`)

405.description: A method this route does not serve (`method_not_allowed`); carries `Allow`

422.description: The name is not an interface name, or the entry is not a WireGuard one (`validation_failed`)

500.description: The stored map holds an entry this build cannot read (`settings_invalid`), or mosd failed to answer (`settings_io`, `mosd_failed`)

504.description: The bounded call to mosd timed out (`mosd_timeout`); the operation may still be running

post.summary: Add one peer to a WireGuard tunnel.
post.description:
Answers **404** when `iface` names no declared interface, checked before
anything is written. A duplicate public key is **409** with code
`peer_exists`; a malformed peer is **422**.

201.description: The peer was added; the body carries it back

401.description: No stored bearer token or authenticated browser session (`not_authenticated`)

403.description: A browser session mutation omitted or supplied the wrong CSRF token (`csrf_invalid`)

404.description: No `network` entry has that name (`settings_not_found`); nothing is written

405.description: A method this route does not serve (`method_not_allowed`); carries `Allow`

409.description: A stored peer already carries that public key (`peer_exists`); the key is this collection's identity, so the entry is not replaced silently

422.description: The name is not an interface name, the entry is not a WireGuard one, or the peer is one the reconciler would refuse -- a public key that is not 32 bytes of base64, an allowed IP that is not a CIDR, an endpoint that is not `host:port` (`validation_failed`)

500.description: The stored map holds an entry this build cannot read (`settings_invalid`), or mosd failed to write (`settings_io`, `mosd_failed`)

503.description: The call to mosd could not be made (`mosd_unreachable`); carries `Retry-After`

504.description: The bounded call to mosd timed out (`mosd_timeout`); the operation may still be running

delete.summary: Remove one peer from a tunnel, identified by its public key.
delete.description:
A string that is not 32 bytes of base64 could never be a WireGuard public
key and is **422**. A well-formed key that no stored peer carries is
**404**.

parameters.name: publicKey
parameters.description: The peer's public key, as `GET /api/v1/network/{iface}/peers` returns it: 32 bytes in padded base64. Its alphabet contains `/` and `+`, so a key carrying either is percent-encoded

204.description: The peer was removed; the reconciler has re-rendered the tunnel without it

401.description: No stored bearer token or authenticated browser session (`not_authenticated`)

403.description: A browser session mutation omitted or supplied the wrong CSRF token (`csrf_invalid`)

404.description: No `network` entry has that name, or no peer of it carries that key (`settings_not_found`)

405.description: A method this route does not serve (`method_not_allowed`); carries `Allow`

422.description: The interface name is not one, the entry is not a WireGuard one, or the path segment is not a WireGuard public key at all (`validation_failed`)

500.description: The stored map holds an entry this build cannot read (`settings_invalid`), or mosd failed to write (`settings_io`, `mosd_failed`)

503.description: The call to mosd could not be made (`mosd_unreachable`); carries `Retry-After`

504.description: The bounded call to mosd timed out (`mosd_timeout`); the operation may still be running

200.description: Setup and browser authentication state

500.description: The access settings could not be read

503.description: mosd is unavailable

post.summary: Authenticate a browser and create its HttpOnly session cookie.

401.description: The password is incorrect

409.description: The device still requires first-run setup

422.description: The JSON body has the wrong shape

401.description: No API credential was supplied

403.description: The browser CSRF token is absent or invalid

get.summary: Read the settings tree at a dot-path.
get.description:
The dot-path is the resource identifier. Secrets are redacted in the
response. An empty path returns the whole tree. Answers **404** when the
path names nothing and **422** when it is not a well-formed dot-path.

200.description: The value at the dot-path, redacted

401.description: No stored bearer token or authenticated browser session (`not_authenticated`)

405.description: A method this route does not serve (`method_not_allowed`); carries `Allow`

422.description: mosd rejected the dot-path (`settings_rejected`)

500.description: mosd failed to answer (`settings_io`, `mosd_failed`)

503.description: The call to mosd could not be made (`mosd_unreachable`); carries `Retry-After`

504.description: The bounded call to mosd timed out (`mosd_timeout`); the operation may still be running

put.summary: Write one scalar setting by dot-path.
put.description:
Accepts four paths and no others: `hostname`, `access.ssh.enabled`,
`container.enabled` and `mqtt.enabled`. Any other path is refused.

Answers **202** with the queued task id on success. Takes a bearer token.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The settings dot-path to write: `hostname`, `access.ssh.enabled`, `container.enabled` or `mqtt.enabled`

202.description: The value was persisted and its scoped reconciliation was queued

401.description: No stored bearer token or authenticated browser session (`not_authenticated`)

403.description: A browser session mutation omitted or supplied the wrong CSRF token (`csrf_invalid`)

404.description: The dot-path names no root the settings schema has (`settings_not_found`)

405.description: A method this route does not serve (`method_not_allowed`); carries `Allow`

409.description: A dot-path that exists and that this route does not write (`settings_read_only`)

422.description: The body carries the redaction sentinel, or is the wrong shape for this setting, or the dot-path is malformed (`validation_failed`); or mosd rejected the write (`settings_rejected`)

500.description: mosd failed to write (`settings_io`, `mosd_failed`)

503.description: The call to mosd could not be made (`mosd_unreachable`); carries `Retry-After`

504.description: The bounded call to mosd timed out (`mosd_timeout`); the operation may still be running

post.summary:
First-run setup: set the admin password, optionally a hostname and network
entries, and mint an API token.
post.description:
**Unauthenticated**, because it creates the device's first credential.
Answers **409** once a password exists, which closes it permanently.

Everything is validated before anything is written; a rejected request
leaves the device untouched and still in setup mode. On success the writes
run in the order hostname, network, `access.webAdmin`, token.

Answers **200** with the minted token secret, returned once. Unlike the
browser wizard, this route always mints one: a caller driving setup over
the API wants API access.

201.description: The device is configured; the body carries a newly minted API token, which is not recoverable afterwards

405.description: A method this route does not serve (`method_not_allowed`); carries `Allow`

409.description: The device already has an admin password, so it is not in setup mode (`already_configured`). Change the password with `POST /api/v1/actions/change-password`

422.description: The body is not this shape, the password is under 8 bytes, the hostname is not a hostname, a `network` key is not an interface name, a static address is not IPv4 CIDR notation, or a relational rule refuses the resulting map -- a VLAN parent or a bridge port that is not a declared entry, a bridge port carrying addressing, a port claimed twice (`validation_failed`); or mosd rejected a write (`settings_rejected`). Nothing is written on any of them

500.description: Hashing the password failed (`hash_failed`), the stored token list could not be read (`settings_invalid`), no free token id was drawn (`mint_failed`), or mosd failed to write (`settings_io`, `mosd_failed`)

503.description: The call to mosd could not be made (`mosd_unreachable`); carries `Retry-After`

504.description: The bounded call to mosd timed out (`mosd_timeout`); the operation may still be running

get.description:
Each entry carries the fingerprint that identifies it for removal. The
response also carries a `notice`: every authorized key grants root.

200.description: The stored keys, each with the fingerprint that is its `DELETE` path segment, and the notice every client of this collection is told

401.description: No stored bearer token or authenticated browser session (`not_authenticated`)

405.description: A method this route does not serve (`method_not_allowed`); carries `Allow`

500.description: The stored list could not be read as a key list (`settings_invalid`), or mosd failed to answer (`settings_io`, `mosd_failed`)

503.description: The call to mosd could not be made (`mosd_unreachable`); carries `Retry-After`

504.description: The bounded call to mosd timed out (`mosd_timeout`); the operation may still be running

post.description:
The key line is validated as submitted; a malformed line is **422**.

**Every authorized key grants root.** `AuthorizedKeysFile` is `%u`-expanded
over one shared list, so the response carries a `notice` saying so
alongside the created entry.

201.description: The key was authorized; the body carries it canonicalised, with its fingerprint and the notice

400.description: The body is not JSON, or not this shape (`request_invalid`)

401.description: No stored bearer token or authenticated browser session (`not_authenticated`)

403.description: A browser session mutation omitted or supplied the wrong CSRF token (`csrf_invalid`)

405.description: A method this route does not serve (`method_not_allowed`); carries `Allow`

409.description: A stored key already carries that public key (`key_exists`), or the device already holds the maximum number of keys (`key_limit_reached`); the collection's current state is what refuses the request, not the body

422.description: The line is not an authorized key, or the resulting list is one the sshd reconciler would refuse (`validation_failed`); or mosd rejected the write (`settings_rejected`)

500.description: The stored list could not be read as a key list (`settings_invalid`), or mosd failed to write (`settings_io`, `mosd_failed`)

503.description: The call to mosd could not be made (`mosd_unreachable`); carries `Retry-After`

504.description: The bounded call to mosd timed out (`mosd_timeout`); the operation may still be running

delete.summary: Remove one authorized SSH key by its fingerprint.
delete.description:
The fingerprint is the only accepted identifier; the key text is not.
Answers **404** when no authorized key carries it.

parameters.name: fingerprint
parameters.description: The key's fingerprint, as `GET /api/v1/ssh/authorized-keys` returns it: `SHA256:` and 43 base64 characters. Its alphabet contains `/`, so a fingerprint carrying one is percent-encoded

204.description: The key was removed; the reconciler has re-rendered the authorized-keys file without it

401.description: No stored bearer token or authenticated browser session (`not_authenticated`)

403.description: A browser session mutation omitted or supplied the wrong CSRF token (`csrf_invalid`)

404.description: No stored key has that fingerprint (`settings_not_found`). Well-formed and absent, which is a different answer from malformed

405.description: A method this route does not serve (`method_not_allowed`); carries `Allow`

422.description: The path segment is not a fingerprint at all (`validation_failed`)

500.description: The stored list could not be read as a key list (`settings_invalid`), or mosd failed to write (`settings_io`, `mosd_failed`)

503.description: The call to mosd could not be made (`mosd_unreachable`); carries `Retry-After`

504.description: The bounded call to mosd timed out (`mosd_timeout`); the operation may still be running

get.summary: Read the live-state tree at a dot-path.
get.description:
Live state is observed, not configured, and is a separate root from
settings. Read-only: there is no write counterpart. Answers **404** when
the path names nothing and **422** when it is not a well-formed dot-path.

200.description: The value at the dot-path, redacted

401.description: No stored bearer token or authenticated browser session (`not_authenticated`)

405.description: A method this route does not serve (`method_not_allowed`); carries `Allow`

422.description: mosd rejected the dot-path (`settings_rejected`); a dot-path that does not resolve is the 404 above

500.description: mosd failed to answer (`settings_io`, `mosd_failed`)

503.description: The call to mosd could not be made (`mosd_unreachable`); carries `Retry-After`

504.description: The bounded call to mosd timed out (`mosd_timeout`); the operation may still be running

get.summary: List mosd's bounded apply-task history, oldest first.

401.description: No stored bearer token or authenticated browser session (`not_authenticated`)

405.description: A method this route does not serve (`method_not_allowed`); carries `Allow`

parameters.description: The task id returned by a 202 response

get.summary: List every API token this device holds.
get.description:
Returns each token's id, label and creation time. Secrets are not stored
and are never returned — a token's secret is shown once, when it is
minted.

200.description: The stored tokens: `id`, `name` and `created`, never the digest and never the plaintext

401.description: No stored bearer token or authenticated browser session (`not_authenticated`)

405.description: A method this route does not serve (`method_not_allowed`); carries `Allow`

500.description: The stored list could not be read as a token list (`settings_invalid`), or mosd failed to answer (`settings_io`, `mosd_failed`)

503.description: The call to mosd could not be made (`mosd_unreachable`); carries `Retry-After`

504.description: The bounded call to mosd timed out (`mosd_timeout`); the operation may still be running

post.description:
Takes either a stored bearer token or an authenticated browser session. The
secret is returned once, in this response, and is not retrievable
afterwards.

A signed-in browser can mint the first additional token through this API.

201.description: The token was created; the body carries the plaintext, which is not recoverable afterwards

400.description: The body is not JSON, or not this shape (`request_invalid`)

401.description: No stored bearer token or authenticated browser session (`not_authenticated`)

403.description: A browser session mutation omitted or supplied the wrong CSRF token (`csrf_invalid`)

405.description: A method this route does not serve (`method_not_allowed`); carries `Allow`

409.description: The device already holds the maximum number of tokens (`token_limit_reached`); revoke one first

422.description: The name is empty, over 256 bytes, or holds a control character (`validation_failed`)

500.description: The stored list could not be read as a token list (`settings_invalid`), no free id was drawn (`mint_failed`), or mosd failed to answer (`settings_io`, `mosd_failed`)

503.description: The call to mosd could not be made (`mosd_unreachable`); carries `Retry-After`

504.description: The bounded call to mosd timed out (`mosd_timeout`); the operation may still be running

delete.summary: Revoke one API token by its id.
delete.description:
Takes effect on the next request; the token set is read per request.
Answers **404** when no token carries that id.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The token id, as `POST /api/v1/tokens` returned it: 1 to 64 lowercase hex characters

204.description: The token was revoked; it stops being accepted on the next request

401.description: No stored bearer token or authenticated browser session (`not_authenticated`)

403.description: A browser session mutation omitted or supplied the wrong CSRF token (`csrf_invalid`)

404.description: No stored token carries that id (`settings_not_found`). Well-formed and absent, which is a different answer from malformed

405.description: A method this route does not serve (`method_not_allowed`); carries `Allow`

422.description: The id is not a token id at all (`validation_failed`)

500.description: The stored list could not be read as a token list (`settings_invalid`), or mosd failed to answer (`settings_io`, `mosd_failed`)

503.description: The call to mosd could not be made (`mosd_unreachable`); carries `Retry-After`

504.description: The bounded call to mosd timed out (`mosd_timeout`); the operation may still be running

get.description:
Asks mosd's `GetUpdateState`, which queries RAUC and re-derives the
lifecycle first — this is the polling surface for a UI watching a check,
download or install, and it is never answered from a stale record.

200.description: The update state: `lifecycle` (state machine with reason strings, effective policy, safe-to-reboot gate and override), per-slot status, `booted_slot`, `primary`, `pending_not_confirmed`, `install`, `last_mark`

401.description: No stored bearer token or authenticated browser session (`not_authenticated`)

405.description: A method this route does not serve (`method_not_allowed`); carries `Allow`

500.description: mosd failed to answer, e.g. RAUC unreachable (`mosd_failed`)

503.description: The call to mosd could not be made (`mosd_unreachable`); carries `Retry-After`

get.summary: List the API major versions this build serves.

200.description: The major API versions this device serves

405.description: A method this route does not serve (`method_not_allowed`); carries `Allow`

key.description:
One authorized-key line, `<type> <blob>` with an optional trailing
comment: exactly what the pane's field takes, handed to exactly the
same parser.

The entry as it was stored, canonicalised by the parser, carrying the
fingerprint that is now its `DELETE` path segment.

notice.description: The same sentence the listing carries.

ApiError.description: The one shape every failure under `/api/` takes.

ApiHealth.description:
The body of `GET /api/v1/health`.

`apid` and `mosd` are always present. `checkedAt` is present only on the
reachable answer and `detail` only on the unreachable one.

apid.description:
Always `"ok"`: a request that got a body was served by an apid that is
up.

checkedAt.description:
Whole seconds since boot, at the moment the probe answered.

The same value and spelling `GET /api/v1/state/uptime` serves.

detail.description: Why the probe did not complete, in the words of whatever refused it.

mosd.description: `"ok"` when the probe completed, `"unreachable"` when it did not.

ApiTokenSummary.description:
One row of `GET /api/v1/tokens`.

Carries no secret: the token's plaintext appears in exactly one response,
when it is minted, and never again.

created.description:
Seconds since the UNIX epoch as the device clock read them at the mint.

**A label, never a deadline.** No unit on this image syncs a clock, so
the reading may be wrong by any amount and 0 means the clock was unset.
Tokens do not expire; revocation is the whole lifecycle (§3.2).

id.description:
The token's stable identity, which is also its `DELETE` path segment.
Not secret: it is a lookup key, and §3.2 puts it on the wire for that.

name.description: The operator's label, the only thing that tells one token from another.

comment.description: The operator's label, absent when the key was stored without one.

fingerprint.description:
This entry's `DELETE` path segment: `SHA256:` followed by the unpadded
base64 of the SHA-256 digest of the decoded blob — the string
`ssh-keygen -lf` prints.

`null` for a stored line whose blob does not decode. Nothing this route
writes can be in that state -- `parse_authorized_key` refuses it -- but
the settings file is an editable file on STATE, so a list read back is
not necessarily a list this API wrote.

key.description:
Canonical `<type> <blob>` key text, with the comment in its own field
-- what the parser stored, and not what was submitted.

AuthorizedKeyList.description:
`GET /api/v1/ssh/authorized-keys` response body.

An object and not a bare array, because of `notice`: the sentence is a
property of the collection rather than of any entry, and the contract
requires it on the listing **and** on the add. A client that only ever adds keys must still be told what a key
grants.

keys.description: Every stored key, in stored order.

notice.description: Why a key added here is not a key with limited access.

BridgeParameters.description: The parameters of a software bridge.

ports.description:
Names of the `network` entries enslaved to this bridge. **Each must be
a declared entry, must carry no addressing of its own, and must not be
a port of another bridge**; a body breaking any of those is refused at
422 with the rule's own sentence.

currentPassword.description: The password being replaced, verified before anything is written.

bundlePath.description:
Absolute path of the bundle to install. Omitted = the staged bundle
the last fetch/import verified (the lifecycle's `bundle`).

MarkRequest.description:
`POST /api/v1/update/mark` request body: mosd's offered vocabulary,
verbatim.

slot.description:
`booted` or `other`. Concrete slot names and `active` are refused by
mosd — activation is the installer's job.

MarkResponse.description: The mark's answer: RAUC's resolved slot name and message.

name.description: The label the new token is listed under.

MintedToken.description:
`POST /api/v1/tokens` response body: the one place a plaintext token
appears.

id.description: The new token's identity, for a later `DELETE`.

name.description: The label as it was submitted.

token.description:
The whole token, `mos_<id>_<secret>`.

**It appears here and nowhere else, ever.** Only the SHA-256 digest is
stored, so a token that is lost is replaced and never recovered -- the
posture `access.device` already takes.

NetworkInterface.description: One `network` entry, as the document describes it.

dhcp.description: Whether the interface acquires its address via DHCP.

kind.description:
`physical`, `vlan`, `bridge` or `wireguard`. Absent means `physical`.

The block below is authoritative and the interface name is not:
`eth0.100` is a convention, not a declaration.

oneOf.description:
Static addressing, used when `dhcp` is false. Absent is an interface
with no addressing at all, which is what a bridge port must be.

configured.description:
The declared settings map. This is desired configuration, not proof of
link health.

observed.description: The current view reported by systemd-networkd.

RebootOverride.description: The armed override, as mosd recorded it.

seconds.description:
Override TTL in seconds: at least 1, at most the policy's
`overrideMaxSeconds` (never above 3600).

ResourceValue.description:
The body of a resource `GET`: the value at the dot-path, as mosd holds it.

Any JSON value: a dot-path can name a subtree, an array or a scalar.

Secrets are replaced by the string `"<redacted>"`, which a client can
receive anywhere inside the body. Every field named `psk`, `passwordHash`,
`password_hash`, `hash` or `privateKey` carries the sentinel instead of its
value, at any depth and inside arrays, and so does the whole body when the
dot-path names one of those fields directly.

The sentinel is read-only: writing it back is refused at **422** rather
than stored, because storing it would destroy the credential.

csrfToken.description: Returned only for an authenticated browser session.

SettingsWrite.description:
The body of a settings `PUT`: the value to write, and nothing around it.

A bare JSON value, the same shape `GET` answers.

The schema is wide because the dot-path decides what is acceptable. What
is actually accepted is narrow: a JSON string for `hostname`, `true` or
`false` for the three switches. Anything else is **422**.

SetupRequest.description:
`POST /api/v1/setup` request body.

No `confirm` member, unlike the form the wizard posts: that field exists so
a human who mistyped a password into a box they cannot read is told before
it becomes the only credential on the device. A client that built a JSON
body knows what it sent, and a second copy of the same string proves
nothing about it.

hostname.description:
The hostname to apply. Absent leaves the stored one alone.

Not trimmed, for the reason `PUT /api/v1/settings/hostname` gives: a
client that built a JSON string chose its bytes, and silently writing
something other than what it sent is the worse answer.

network.description:
`network` entries to declare, merged into the stored map by name.

An entry whose name is already declared is replaced whole; one that is
not is added. Entries the body does not name are left alone.

password.description:
The admin password to set. At least 8 bytes, the floor the wizard and
the change-password route enforce.

csrfToken.description: CSRF token for the browser session created by setup.

token.description:
The whole token, `mos_<id>_<secret>`.

**It appears here and nowhere else, ever**, exactly as the mint route's
does: only the SHA-256 digest is stored. The id is not a separate
member because it is the token's own second segment, so a caller that
holds this string can address it for a later `DELETE` without being
told it twice.

address.description: Interface address in CIDR notation, e.g. `192.168.1.10/24`.

gateway.description: Default gateway address; absent for a link with no route of its own.

TaskAccepted.description: A persisted settings write whose reconciliation continues asynchronously.

TaskRecord.description: One queued apply lifecycle, shared by the D-Bus client and HTTP surface.

password.description:
The password to open the channel with: 8 to 72 bytes, and no NUL,
newline or carriage return.

oneOf.description:
The newest usable retained generation, or the newest unusable one with
a reason when no generation passes validation.

mode.description: `builtIn` when no custom bundle is active, otherwise `custom`.

UpdateState.description:
The update state document, verbatim from mosd: `lifecycle` (state machine,
policy, reboot gate), per-slot status, `booted_slot`, `primary`,
`pending_not_confirmed`, `install` and `last_mark`.

VlanParameters.description: The 802.1Q parameters of a VLAN interface.

parent.description:
Name of the `network` entry this VLAN sits on. **It must be a declared
entry**; a body naming one that is not is refused at 422.

WifiNetworkEntry.description:
One known WiFi network, in both directions.


`psk` differs by direction. On the way **in** it is the pre-shared key. On
the way **out** it is `"<redacted>"` whenever a key is stored. A body
carrying the sentinel back is refused at **422** rather than written.

hidden.description: Whether the network hides its SSID.

psk.description:
The pre-shared key; absent for an open network, `"<redacted>"` on
every read of a network that has one.

ssid.description: The network name, which is also this entry's `DELETE` path segment.

WireguardParameters.description:
The parameters of a WireGuard tunnel.

There is no private-key member and there never will be: this subtree is
served over `GET /api/v1/settings/network`, so a key in it is a key
published to every client. The private key lives in a mode-0640 file on the
device and only its public half is surfaced, through
`GET /api/v1/state/network` and the rotate action.

listenPort.description: UDP port to listen on; absent lets the kernel pick one.

peers.description:
The far ends of the tunnel. A `PUT` of this interface replaces them;
the peer collection route edits them one at a time.

WireguardPeerEntry.description: One far end of a WireGuard tunnel, in both directions.

endpoint.description: `host:port` to send to, for a peer this end initiates to.

persistentKeepalive.description: Keepalive interval in seconds, for a peer behind NAT.

publicKey.description:
The peer's X25519 public key: 32 bytes in padded base64. It is also
this entry's `DELETE` path segment, and its alphabet contains `/`, so a
key carrying one is percent-encoded there.

WireguardRotation.description:
The body of a successful key rotation: the public half, and nothing else.

There is no `privateKey` member here and there will not be one. The private
half never leaves mosd — there is no read-back route for the private key,
ever; not redacted-on-read, nonexistent — so this struct is the whole of
what a rotation can answer.

publicKey.description: The new base64 X25519 public key, which is what the far end needs.
